criteria.criterion: a pure helper derives `instance` from a base URL; different deployments differ, and equivalent spellings of one deployment (trailing slash / case / default port) agree

`Backend` DECLARES `remote_ref()`, both concrete backends IMPLEMENT it, and each returns a `RemoteRef` whose `vendor` and `remote_id` are correct and whose `instance` is EXACTLY THE VALUE THE CONSTRUCTOR WAS GIVEN — asserted against the REAL backends, constructed in the test with an EXPLICIT instance argument and no ambient config; a backend constructed WITHOUT the argument returns the empty default
two backends at different base URLs yield unequal `RemoteRef`s for the same `remote_id`
the chosen `instance` source is documented, INCLUDING what happens when the base URL changes, and including that this story does not persist a `RemoteRef` anywhere

BOTH ADRs named in Scope (0055 and 0035) and `RemoteRef`'s docstring are AMENDED to state that `instance` does NOT prevent local-id collision between two same-vendor deployments and that `vendor` already separates Cloud from DC
a test pins that known limitation, so it cannot be silently assumed fixed
no new operator-facing config key is introduced, `_jira_key_to_local_id` is unchanged, and no `remote_ref()` call is added to any pass

`remote_ref()` resolves NO configuration when called — the `instance` value arrives via the constructor from the `build_backend` factory, and the contract test constructs both real backends with no config context to prove it
the contract test covers `remote_ref()` for the REAL backends, closing the gap where `backend_support.FakeBackend` implemented a port member production did not
